title: Polydatin as a Potential Multitarget Modulator of Oncogenic Signaling, Protein Homeostasis, and Metabolic Stress Pathways
content: Polydatin exhibited high binding affinities toward several key targets, including H-Ras GTPase (ΔG ≈ −10.0 kcal/mol), RAC-β serine/threonine protein kinase/AKT2 (ΔG ≈ −9.8 kcal/mol), heat shock protein HSP90-α (ΔG ≈ −9.8 kcal/mol), retinoic acid receptor γ (ΔG ≈ −10.0 kcal/mol), aldose reductase (ΔG ≈ −9.7 kcal/mol), and hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (ΔG ≈ −9.6 kcal/mol). Binding mode analysis revealed stable interaction networks driven by hydrogen bonding, π–π stacking, and hydrophobic contacts with functionally relevant residues, suggesting modulation of both catalytic and allosteric regions. Notably, strong affinity toward traditionally challenging targets such as H-Ras and HSP90 highlights polydatin’s potential as a multitarget natural compound, capable of modulating oncogenic signaling pathways (PI3K/AKT, MAPK), metabolic pathways, and proteostasis networks. These findings provide a mechanistic rationale for the pleiotropic biological activities of polydatin and support further in vitro and in vivo investigations for therapeutic development. The high binding affinities across all targets and engagement of functionally critical residues support the hypothesis that polydatin acts as a multitarget modulator of oncogenic, metabolic, and stress-response pathways. Although docking results indicate strong multitarget potential, further in vitro and in vivo studies are needed to validate these findings.
